subject: Connector runway: control-plane / data-plane sequence review for on-prem VPC integration
messages:
From: Tanya Okafor <tanya@blueharbor.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.com
Cc: eng@blueharbor.com
Date: 2027-04-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Connector runway: initial control/data sequence for on-prem VPC

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We sketched a first-pass sequence diagram for the connector runway between our on-prem VPC and Redwood's private control plane. The goals: keep control-plane traffic (heartbeats, model manifest sync) on an authenticated mutual-TLS channel to Redwood control endpoints, and route inference (data-plane) traffic via a customer NAT through our egress firewall to a dedicated data-plane ingress (LB) in the region.

High-level asks:
- Can you validate the attached sequence diagram for any missing control-plane messages or timing assumptions?
- Any constraints around long-lived KV cache warmup or prefix rehydration we should account for during cutover?
- Do you expect any extra NAT or port requirements beyond standard HTTPS (443) for model fetches or tracing?

I've attached the PNG and a short runbook draft. Would appreciate concrete callouts so we can fold them into our change window on May 4.

Thanks,
Tanya

From: jasmine_liu@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Connector runway: initial control/data sequence for on-prem VPC

Tanya —

Thanks for the diagram and the runbook. I pulled this into a quick sanity pass with Rishi, Kim and Jonas; attaching a PDF with a few markup notes (controlplane_flow_v1.pdf) and an annotated sequence_diagram_v1.png. High-level notes up front:

- Control-plane: agrees that mTLS to our control endpoints is the right pattern. We recommend a short-lived client cert rotation (30d) and an automated renewal hook in your key management flow; otherwise watch for a cert-expiry-driven outage.
- Heartbeats: our heartbeat TTL is 90s by default; if you plan aggressive scaling that spins nodes frequently, set client-side backoff to avoid stampeding reconnects.
- KV cache: we do prefix pre-warm for frequently used models but full KV state is loaded lazily. For cutover, plan a warmup window of about 10-15 minutes per tenant to avoid initial latency spikes.
- Egress/NAT: data-plane (inference traffic) is HTTPS (443). Control plane uses HTTPS over mTLS on 443 as well. No additional ports required for normal operation. If you have deep packet inspection that terminates TLS, we'll need a mutual-auth friendly proxy — option details below.

Open questions for your side:
1) Do you expect any managed edge proxies that will terminate TLS before the NAT? (That would require a proxy trust bundle agreement.)
2) Are you planning BGP or static routes for the control/data egress? BGP advertised prefixes might simplify firewall rules.

Next steps: Rishi suggested a short call to walk through the markup and confirm runbook actions. Can we do 30 minutes Friday (Apr 16) 10:00-10:30 PT? If that works for you we'll bring a small runbook checklist and a pre-cutover validation script.

— Jasmine

On Wed, Apr 14, 2027 at 11:03 AM jasmine_liu@redwood.com wrote:
> - Heartbeats: our heartbeat TTL is 90s by default; if you plan aggressive scaling that spins nodes frequently, set client-side backoff to avoid stampeding reconnects.

Adding a couple of operational tweaks from the runtime side:

- If the on-prem cluster has very bursty infer requests, enable our incremental KV streaming option. That reduces the first-token latency for cold prefixes by streaming the most-used keysets first. It adds a small (sub-5ms) CPU overhead per request but avoids large warmup stalls.
- For observability: include the X-Request-Tag header (we use it to stitch traces across control/data flows). That header is permitted over TLS and doesn't change port requirements.
- Failover policy: recommend policy 'prefer-dedicated' for your initial cutover so if a data-plane LB is unreachable we fail into a lower-cap model rather than full rejection. We'll document expected error-codes in the runbook.

I'll prepare a short validation script for your ops team that checks: cert rotation endpoint, heartbeat intervals, KV prefix counts, and a sample inference call that measures cold vs warmed latency. Dropping the draft scripts to INF-8723 (Jira).

— Rishi
